questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
What is an example of a negative externality?

options.A: the non-provision of public goods by the market
options.B: indirect taxation that fails to internalise the external cost
options.C: monopoly power leading to reduced output and a higher price
options.D: the production of a good that has a harmful effect on a third party

questions.questionText: A government deregulates several industries with the aim to increase allocative and productive efficiency. Which change makes it less likely that the government will meet its aim?

options.A: an increase in the availability of cheap loans to start new businesses
options.B: an increase in merger and takeover activity in the industries
options.C: an increase in information about prices for consumers available on the internet
options.D: a reduction in fixed costs in the deregulated industries

questions.questionText: A rational consumer maximises satisfaction by buying three units of good X and four units of good Y which are the same dollar price. What does this indicate?

options.A: Marginal utility per dollar spent is equal for both goods.
options.B: The total utility of 3X is equal to the total utility of 4Y.
options.C: The consumer should buy one more unit of good X to maximise utility.
options.D: Good Y has greater marginal utility than good X.

questions.questionText: What does a budget line on an indifference curve diagram show?

options.A: the amount that a household has available to spend plotted against time
options.B: the combinations of two goods that can be purchased when all income is spent
options.C: the difference between a government’s income and expenditure plotted against time
options.D: the relationship between the price of a good and the amount demanded

questions.questionText: Firm X, which currently specialises in producing cars, takes over firm Y, which owns a number of car retail outlets. How may this be described?

options.A: horizontal integration

questions.questionText: In large cities there are streets where many sellers of similar hot foods compete for sales. Which type of market structure does this represent?

options.A: monopoly

questions.questionText: A firm always operates with economies of scale in the long run. What is the shape of its long-run average cost curve?

options.A: It is horizontal.

questions.questionText: A multinational firm seeks to minimise costs and maximise profits. What would least assist the multinational to achieve these objectives?

options.A: achieving a near monopoly status to control outputs and prices
options.B: locating the firm’s home base in a country with a low level of corporation tax
options.C: operating as a member of a cartel with production quotas
options.D: owning subsidiary firms in different countries to achieve economies of scale

questions.questionText: What is the most likely combination of income elasticity of demand and price elasticity of demand that explains why a firm can make higher profits in specialised luxury product markets? income elasticity price elasticity of demand of demand

options.A: high high

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s cost and revenue curves. cost, revenue MC AC AR MR O output The firm embarks on a single successful $100 million advertising campaign. How will this affect its costs and revenue curves? MR curve AR curve MC curve AC curve

options.A: shifts to right shifts to right shifts up unchanged
options.B: shifts to right shifts to right unchanged shifts up

questions.questionText: In which circumstances are a firm’s objectives most likely to differ from profit maximisation?

options.A: when a firm finances new investment largely by retained profits
options.B: where firms are companies with very active shareholders
options.C: where investment banks make takeovers easy to implement
options.D: when a firm has many shareholders and is managed by employees

questions.questionText: Which combination of policies is most likely to reduce the inequality of the income distribution? availability direct tax indirect tax of benefit

options.A: decrease decrease decrease

questions.questionText: To tackle pollution, some governments set standards, such as production limits, while others use tradeable pollution permits. What is a correct comparison of the two approaches?

options.A: Standards give more incentive for continued pollution reduction.
options.B: Standards make greater use of the market mechanism.
options.C: Tradeable pollution permits are simpler to devise and administer.
options.D: Tradeable pollution permits provide a more equitable treatment of firms.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an economy’s Lorenz curve (VW). W cumulative 45° % of income X Y V 0 100 cumulative % of population The area of Y is three times bigger than the area of X. What is the value of the economy’s Gini coefficient?

options.A: 1 B 1 C 3 D 4

questions.questionText: What will not shift the demand curve for labour to the right?

options.A: improvement in marginal productivity of labour
options.B: increase in demand for the product
options.C: increase in the price of the product

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an individual’s supply of labour curve. S hourly wage ($) w x z y number of hours per week He is offered a job which would require him to work a standard 40-hour week. Which area measures the amount he would need to get him to accept this job offer?

options.A: w + z B x + y C x + y – z D w + x + z + y

questions.questionText: The aggregate demand in country X is calculated by the equation AD = C + I + (X – M). Four students are asked to fill in the two gaps in the following sentence describing the economy of country X. ‘Country X is ......1...... economy ......2...... a government.’ Which student is correct? gap 1 gap 2

options.A: a closed with

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the Kuznets curve. income inequality Q R P S O per capita income Which statement is correct with respect to the description of an economy and the corresponding letter on the Kuznets curve?

options.A: P is a market economy.
options.D: S is an economy with a Gini coefficient = 0.

questions.questionText: When measuring the value of total output of a country, economists use the concept of value added. What could explain this?

options.A: They want to avoid double counting.
options.B: They want to avoid the impact of inflation.
options.C: They want to find the value of the hidden economy.
options.D: They want to include indirect taxes and subsidies.

questions.questionText: A government uses personal disposable income per head as a measure of the standard of living. What does this measure not take into account?

options.A: changes in the average price level

questions.questionText: Which policy would be most likely to increase employment?

options.A: decreasing duties on imports

questions.questionText: Low income countries that approached the IMF for loan assistance were usually required to introduce structural adjustment programmes (SAPs) which involve policies to promote a free-market economy. Which action would have been included in a SAP?

options.A: deregulation of agricultural markets
options.D: restrictions and regulations on the flow of international capital

questions.questionText: In a closed economy with no government there is an initial equilibrium level of national income of $500 billion. The economy’s households always spend a constant fraction of every $1 of income they receive. When investment spending increases by $20 billion the economy moves to a new equilibrium level of national income of $600 billion. What is the marginal propensity to consume of the economy’s households?
The Keynesian theory states that the demand for money (Md) is influenced by the personal level of income (L ) and by the rate of interest (L ) so that
What are the assumptions made by Keynesians in relation to wages and investment? wages investment

options.A: flexible interest rates elastic

questions.questionText: What are the characteristics of most developing economies? ratio of government average debt to GDP propensity to save

options.A: high high

questions.questionText: Money given by the US government to certain African countries to fight AIDS/HIV requires their governments to purchase expensive drugs from the US rather than cheaper products from South Africa, India or Brazil. What is this an example of?

options.A: bilateral aid

questions.questionText: Why do economists draw a distinction between economic development and economic growth?

options.A: because a country’s stage of economic development depends on its level of output rather than its growth rate
options.B: because it is the allocation rather than the overall level of a country’s resources which determines its economic well-being
options.C: because of the concern about quality of life rather than quantity of output
options.D: because the prime determinant of economic development is investment rather than consumption

questions.questionText: In an economy operating below full employment, which combination of changes will definitely result in an increase in national income?

options.A: a fall in the rate of taxation together with a rise in the saving rate
options.B: a rise in government expenditure together with a fall in the propensity to import
options.C: a rise in investment expenditure together with a rise in the rate of taxation
